uchoice.notes: Source read at commit 0a84df9, the only commit whose plugin.json carries the installed 2.0.0; it is also the repository head, so nothing had to be settled. The installed res folder is byte-identical to the repository's. The seven jacks and the seven buttons are in panel order, top to bottom, which is unusual for this maker: gchoice in the same plugin wires its jacks bottom up. Nothing in this module is given a name: every configParam is called with only an id, a range and a default, and there is no configInput or configOutput at all, so Rack's hover tooltips are blank throughout. Two faults in the code. First, dataFromJson at line 88 reads the saved selection with json_is_true on a value written as json_integer, which is false for any integer, so current is restored as 0 whatever was saved; the button states beside it are written as json_boolean and do restore correctly. Second, when the chooser is handed an empty list — every input switched out — utility.cpp returns 0, so a trigger in that state lights the first input's lamp even though that input is out of the draw; the output is separately forced to 0V by line 127. Neither the inputs nor the output is given a family, because a mult of this kind carries whatever is patched into it.

lines: Passes one of seven inputs through to the output and draws a new one on each trigger, with a bell curve deciding which input is likely
Scales the voltage at the mean cv jack before it is added to the mean slider, 0 to 0.6, so at its top 10V moves the centre of the curve across all seven inputs
Sets which input the curve is centred on, 0 at the bottom of its travel for the lowest jack up to 6 for the highest; it starts at 3, the middle jack
Sets how wide the curve is, 0.5 to 3.5 measured in jack spacings, so turned down the draw nearly always lands on the centre input and turned up it reaches the ends
Scales the voltage at the spread cv jack before it is added to the spread knob, 0 to 0.35, so at its top 10V covers the whole of that knob's travel
One of the seven signals the module draws between; its voltage reaches the output for as long as the draw is on it
Moves the centre of the curve, scaled by the mean cv att knob and added to the mean slider, with the total held between the lowest and highest jack
Widens or narrows the curve, scaled by the spread cv att knob and added to the spread knob, with the total held between 0.5 and 3.5
A trigger draws a new input; it fires above 2V and rearms below 0.1V
Carries the voltage of whichever input the last draw landed on
Note — the module starts on the middle input and passes it through; a trigger at trig is what makes it draw again
Note — the lamp beside each jack shows how likely that input is to be drawn, and the one the draw is on is lit fully
Note — a draw that falls off either end of the seven is thrown away and the choice is left where it was, so with spread turned up some triggers pass without changing anything
Note — the chosen input is not written into the patch file, so a saved patch reopens on the middle input

gchoice.notes: Source read at commit 0a84df9, the only commit whose plugin.json carries the installed 2.0.0. THE SEVEN SOURCE JACKS ARE WIRED BOTTOM UP: GchoiceWidget adds SOURCE_INPUTS+6 at the top of the column and SOURCE_INPUTS+0 at the bottom, so index order is the reverse of panel order. That is consistent with the rest of the module — the mean slider's top end is 6 and the lamp array is added in the same reversed order — so the curve's centre really does follow the slider up the panel. All four parameters are configured with an empty name and no unit, and there is no configInput or configOutput, so Rack's hover tooltips are blank throughout. The mean slider is a tall SvgSlider declared in plugin.hpp; it has a ParamWidget and a census position, so it can be clicked for help even though the panel art shows nothing where it sits. random_gaussian in utility.cpp rounds a normal deviate to an integer and gchoice.cpp:62 discards anything outside 0 to 6, which is why a wide spread makes some triggers do nothing rather than folding back. The lamps are fed 0.8 times a gaussian, so a probability lamp never reaches full brightness; only the lamp for the chosen input is set to 1, which is how the maker's README says it is meant to read. The module has no dataToJson, so the choice is lost when a patch is saved. The seven source jacks and the output are given no family, because a router of this kind carries whatever is patched into it.
